decisions.decision: Established a manual-merge-over-automation pattern for isolated-worktree wave execution
decisions.rationale: gsd-tools' `worktree.cleanup-wave` unconditionally blocks merging any branch containing file deletions (deliberate, undocumented opt-in gap per its own code comments referencing issues #2852/#3003) — every wave with an intentional file deletion (02.1-01, 02.1-06) required a manual `git merge --no-ff` + hand-resolved conflict instead. When two isolated worktrees both touched the same file in different ways (server-client.integration.test.ts: 02.1-04's EXTERNAL_PATH routing vs 02.1-03's more-correct expiredRecord.id test data), the correct resolution combined both improvements rather than picking one side.

decisions.decision: Added a full lint+test+build+routes+handlers gate on the MERGED result after every wave, not just per-plan verification inside each isolated worktree
decisions.rationale: Wave 3 alone had 3 cross-plan gaps that only a merged-result gate could catch: 02.1-04 touched 3 files 02.1-06 had already deleted (needed manual conflict resolution), 02.1-04 and 02.1-03 both touched server-client.integration.test.ts (content conflict), and 02.1-04's widened routes:check script flagged literals in NEW files 02.1-06 created in its own isolated worktree that 02.1-04 could never have seen. Each isolated worktree's own internal verification was necessarily blind to what its siblings were doing.
